title.en: Swadeshi, revolutionaries and Home Rule in Tamil Nadu
Two ships on the sea to Colombo

text.en: In 1906 two steamships, Gallia and Lavo, began sailing between Thoothukudi and Colombo, owned not by Europeans but by Indians. Their founder, V.O. Chidambaranar, was about to pay a heavy price for that act of defiance.

The partition of Bengal in 1905 led to the Swadeshi Movement, calling on Indians to boycott foreign goods and build national education and enterprise.
In Tamil Nadu leaders like V.O. Chidambaranar, V. Chakkaraiyar and Subramania Bharati held mass meetings, and Tamil was used on the public platform to mobilise people.
Bharati's patriotic songs stirred emotions, and Bipin Chandra Pal's lectures in Madras inspired youth.
In 1906 V.O. Chidambaranar launched the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Thoothukudi with the ships Gallia and Lavo.
With Subramania Siva he led the 1908 strike at the European-owned Coral Mills in Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli.
The two were arrested for sedition, and VOC first received two life imprisonments, treated harshly and made to pull the oil press.
News of the arrest led to riots in Tirunelveli, with the police station and court burnt, and four died in police firing.
Subramania Bharati moved to Pondicherry under French rule, and others like Aurobindo Ghosh and V.V. Subramanianar followed.
Pondicherry sheltered revolutionaries trained at India House in London and in Paris, such as M.P.T. Acharya and V.V. Subramanianar, and papers like India, Vijaya and Suryodayam were published there.
Nilakanta Brahmachari began the secret Bharata Matha Society in 1904, which influenced Vanchinathan of Senkottai.
On 17 June 1911 Vanchinathan shot Robert Ashe, Collector of Tirunelveli, at Maniyachi Junction and then shot himself.
In 1916 Annie Besant, an Irish leader of the Theosophical Society, started the Home Rule League, with G.S. Arundale, B.P. Wadia and C.P. Ramaswamy, and papers New India and Commonweal.
George Joseph, a barrister, led the Home Rule cause in Madurai and was fondly called Rosaappu Durai.

problem.en: Explain V.O. Chidambaranar's role in the Swadeshi Movement.

text.en: He launched the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906 with two ships.

why.en: They ran between Thoothukudi and Colombo.

text.en: He and Subramania Siva led the Coral Mills strike in 1908.
He was arrested for sedition and punished harshly.

why.en: He pulled the oil press in prison.

prompt.en: Why was Pondicherry important to Tamil revolutionaries?

requiredIdeas.en: Safe haven for Bharati, Aurobindo and others

commonMisconceptions.en: Placing the Ashe murder at Pondicherry instead of Maniyachi

points.en: Besant's Home Rule League began in 1916.
